architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created a reusable CopyTextLink component for consistent copy functionality across the UI
architecture_decisions.rationale: The copy functionality was needed in multiple places (starting with the run inspector), so creating a dedicated component ensures consistency, reduces code duplication, and follows the existing component pattern in the primitives directory. The component uses the existing useCopy hook for clipboard operations and follows the same styling conventions as other primitive components.
alternatives_considered: Inline copy button implementation directly in the route component
Extending existing CopyableText component instead of creating new one
Using a third-party clipboard library instead of the custom useCopy hook

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Improved text wrapping and truncation using CSS utility classes and grid layout adjustments
architecture_decisions.rationale: Long text content was overflowing containers without proper wrapping. The solution uses `[overflow-wrap:break-word]` to handle long unbroken strings, `min-w-0` to allow flex children to shrink, and `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_auto]` to create responsive layouts that prevent overflow. This approach maintains the existing Tailwind CSS utility class pattern while fixing specific layout issues.
alternatives_considered: Adding custom CSS classes with specific break-word rules
Using JavaScript to truncate text based on container width
Implementing a custom text truncation component

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added visual feedback for copy operations with icon and text state changes
architecture_decisions.rationale: Users need clear feedback when copy operations succeed. The implementation shows 'Copy' text with a clipboard icon initially, then changes to 'Copied' with a checkmark icon and success color after copying. This follows established UX patterns in the codebase and provides immediate, clear feedback without disrupting the user's workflow.
alternatives_considered: Temporary text color change only without icon change
No visual feedback beyond the clipboard operation

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Placed the copy button in the Property.Label area rather than next to the value
architecture_decisions.rationale: The copy functionality is placed in the label area (right-aligned) to maintain visual hierarchy and prevent the copy button from interfering with the message content display. This keeps the primary content area clean while making the copy action discoverable through its proximity to the 'Message' label.
alternatives_considered: Placing copy button next to the message value
Adding copy button as a floating action button
Using a hover-reveal pattern for the copy button

implementation_summary:
The implementation addresses text display improvements in the run inspector through three key changes. First, a new reusable CopyTextLink component was created in the primitives directory, following the established component architecture pattern. This component leverages the existing useCopy hook for clipboard operations and provides visual feedback through icon and text state changes, ensuring consistency with the UI design system.

Second, layout improvements were made to fix text wrapping issues. The header section was refactored from a flex layout to a grid layout using `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_auto]` to prevent overflow, and `min-w-0` was added to allow proper shrinking of flex children. For the message content, `[overflow-wrap:break-word]` was added alongside the existing `whitespace-pre-wrap` to handle long unbroken strings that previously overflowed containers.

Third, the copy functionality was integrated into the Message property by adding the CopyTextLink component to the Property.Label area. This placement maintains visual hierarchy while making the copy action easily discoverable. The implementation follows the existing code patterns in the route component, including proper TypeScript typing and consistent use of utility classes from the cn helper. These changes collectively improve the user experience for inspecting run details while maintaining code quality and consistency with the existing architecture.
